title: How many retries before a human takes over?
one_liner: There's no agreed limit yet -- and 3 build tasks are blocked until we set one.

recommendation.headline: Set the limit at 2 repeat attempts, then force a human handoff.
recommendation.rationale: Two attempts covers 96% of successful self-resolutions in the logs. Beyond that, resolution rate falls and frustration signals rise. A hard cap closes the open evidence gap and unblocks the routing work.

goals.note: A cap keeps repeat loops from delaying escalation.

title: Give Atlas read access to order history?
one_liner: Broader data access improves answers but widens the exposure surface.

recommendation.headline: Approve, scoped to read-only order status and history only.
recommendation.rationale: In 36 of 40 test chats, order-history access alone was enough to answer the customer without a human. Scoping to read-only status and history keeps that gain while limiting what Atlas can see.

title: Auto-approve refunds under $50?
one_liner: Where the human-in-the-loop line sits — speed for customers vs. spend control for the business.

recommendation.headline: Approve auto-approval up to $50, with a running weekly cap and full audit log.
recommendation.rationale: Simulating the $50 auto-approval rule against 340 recent sub-$50 refund requests matched the human-approved outcome in 312 cases. A running weekly cap and full audit log cover the handful of simulated weeks that drifted past a safe spend limit.

evidence.title: Auto-refund simulation
evidence.note: 312 of 340 sub-$50 refund cases matched the human-approved outcome.

evidence.title: Refund policy v2.1
evidence.note: Auto-approval logic mirrors the $50 threshold already approved in policy.

evidence.title: Weekly cap stress test
